title: Network path was not found
message: A network-related or instance-specific error occurred. (provider: Named Pipes Provider, error: 40)
meaning: The instance was never reached. Name resolution, port, firewall or the Browser service.

title: Incorrect syntax near
message: Incorrect syntax near 'X'.
meaning: Often a compatibility level or version issue rather than a real typo, when the same code works elsewhere.

title: Invalid column name
message: Invalid column name 'X'.
meaning: Typo, wrong alias, or a column that exists in a different environment to the one you are on.

title: Invalid object name
message: Invalid object name 'dbo.X'.
meaning: Wrong database context or schema more often than a missing object.

title: SELECT permission denied
message: The SELECT permission was denied on the object 'X', database 'Y', schema 'dbo'.
meaning: Object-level permission, or a DENY inherited from a role.

title: Conversion failed when converting
message: Conversion failed when converting the varchar value 'abc' to data type int.
meaning: Implicit conversion meeting a value that will not convert. Also a performance smell.

title: CREATE DATABASE permission denied
message: CREATE DATABASE permission denied in database 'master'.
meaning: Needs dbcreator or sysadmin, and it is the same shape for most CREATE permissions.

title: VIEW SERVER STATE permission denied
message: VIEW SERVER STATE permission was denied on object 'server', database 'master'.
meaning: Every interesting DMV is behind this. Database roles cannot reach it.

title: Conflict with a FOREIGN KEY constraint
message: The INSERT statement conflicted with the FOREIGN KEY constraint 'FK_X'.
meaning: The parent row does not exist, or you are deleting one that still has children.

title: Attempt to fetch logical page belongs to a different object
message: Attempt to fetch logical page ... in database ... belongs to object ..., not to object ...
meaning: Allocation corruption. Stop and go to backups.

title: Insufficient system memory
message: There is insufficient system memory in resource pool 'default' to run this query.
meaning: Real memory pressure, or a single query asking for far more than it should.

title: I/O error, the operating system reported a failure
message: The operating system returned error 21 to SQL Server during a read at offset 0x... in file 'X'.
meaning: The storage layer failed the request. This is hardware or driver, not SQL Server.

title: Logical consistency-based I/O error
message: SQL Server detected a logical consistency-based I/O error: incorrect checksum.
meaning: The read succeeded and the page was wrong. Check the backups before anything else.

title: Read-retry succeeded
message: A read of the file 'X' at offset ... succeeded after failing N attempt(s).
meaning: The quiet one. Severity 10 so nothing alerts, and it is the warning before 823 and 824.

title: Not able to access the database under the current security context
message: The server principal "X" is not able to access the database "Y" under the current security context.
meaning: Common in SSMS Object Explorer when a login has no user in one database on the instance.

title: Database is in the middle of a restore
message: Database 'X' cannot be opened. It is in the middle of a restore.
meaning: RESTORING state. The question is whether a restore is running or the database was stranded.

title: Database cannot be opened due to inaccessible files
message: Database 'X' cannot be opened due to inaccessible files or insufficient memory or disk space.
meaning: The files are missing, the service account lost access, or the volume is gone.

title: Could not allocate space, filegroup is full
message: Could not allocate space for object 'X' in database 'Y' because the 'PRIMARY' filegroup is full.
meaning: Data file, not log. Autogrowth off, disk full, or a size cap reached.

title: Deadlock victim
message: Transaction (Process ID 52) was deadlocked on lock resources with another process and has been chosen as the deadlock victim.
meaning: The engine picked the cheaper transaction to kill. The fix is in the access pattern, not the error.

title: Lock request time out period exceeded
message: Lock request time out period exceeded.
meaning: Blocking, not deadlock. Something held a lock longer than the timeout allowed.

title: Cannot insert duplicate key row in unique index
message: Cannot insert duplicate key row in object 'dbo.X' with unique index 'IX_Y'.
meaning: Same as 2627 but from a unique index rather than a primary key.

title: Violation of PRIMARY KEY constraint
message: Violation of PRIMARY KEY constraint 'PK_X'. Cannot insert duplicate key in object 'dbo.Y'.
meaning: A duplicate insert, often a retry that succeeded the first time.

title: String or binary data would be truncated in table
message: String or binary data would be truncated in table 'db.dbo.T', column 'c'. Truncated value: 'X'.
meaning: The 2019 and later version of 8152. It names the table, the column and the value.

title: Restore database is terminating abnormally
message: RESTORE DATABASE is terminating abnormally.
meaning: The companion message, never the cause. The error immediately above it is the real one.

title: The backup set holds a backup of a database other than the existing one
message: The backup set holds a backup of a database other than the existing 'X' database.
meaning: Restoring over a different database needs WITH REPLACE, and deserves a pause first.

title: Cannot open backup device
message: Cannot open backup device 'X'. Operating system error 5(Access is denied.).
meaning: Almost always the SQL Server service account, not your own account, lacking access to the path.

title: Media family on device is incorrectly formed
message: The media family on device 'X' is incorrectly formed. SQL Server cannot process this media family.
meaning: Wrong file, truncated copy, or a backup from a newer version being restored to an older one.

title: Cannot recover the master database
message: Cannot recover the master database. SQL Server is unable to run.
meaning: The instance will not start. Master is damaged, moved, or its permissions changed.

title: Cannot open database requested by the login
message: Cannot open database "X" requested by the login. The login failed.
meaning: The login is fine. The database named in the connection string is missing, offline or not permitted.

title: Cannot open user default database
message: Cannot open user default database. Login failed.
meaning: The login's default database is unavailable. Fixable without touching the database.

title: Database could not be exclusively locked
message: The database could not be exclusively locked to perform the operation.
meaning: Something is connected. Common when setting a database to single user or restoring over it.

title: CREATE FILE encountered operating system error
message: CREATE FILE encountered operating system error 5(Access is denied.) while attempting to open the file 'X'.
meaning: Service account permissions on the target folder, or a path that does not exist.

title: Not a primary database file
message: 'X.mdf' is not a primary database file.
meaning: A corrupt or wrong file being attached, or a file copied while the instance was running.

title: String or binary data would be truncated
message: String or binary data would be truncated.
meaning: Pre-2019 it will not tell you which column. 2019 and later name the column and the value.

title: Query processor ran out of internal resources
message: The query processor ran out of internal resources and could not produce a query plan.
meaning: Nearly always an enormous IN list or a generated query of extreme size.

title: Timeout waiting for memory resources
message: A timeout occurred while waiting for memory resources to execute the query.
meaning: RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE waits. Query memory grants are the thing to look at.

title: Transaction log is full
message: The transaction log for database 'X' is full due to 'LOG_BACKUP'.
meaning: The reason in quotes is the diagnosis, and it is rarely solved by shrinking.

title: Existing connection was forcibly closed
message: A connection was successfully established with the server, but then an error occurred during the login process.
meaning: Not a login problem. The handshake failed before credentials were checked.

title: User already exists in current database
message: User, group, or role 'X' already exists in the current database.
meaning: The classic orphaned user after a restore. The user exists, its SID no longer matches a login.

title: Database principal owns a schema
message: The database principal owns a schema in the database, and cannot be dropped.
meaning: Reassign the schema owner first, then drop the user.

title: Cannot execute as the database principal
message: Cannot execute as the database principal because the principal "dbo" does not exist.
meaning: Usually a database whose owner SID no longer resolves, after a restore or a domain change.

title: SSPI handshake failed
message: SSPI handshake failed with error code 0x8009030c.
meaning: Kerberos or NTLM could not complete. Usually a duplicate or missing SPN, or clock skew.

title: Login from an untrusted domain
message: Login failed. The login is from an untrusted domain and cannot be used with Integrated authentication.
meaning: Windows authentication could not be negotiated, often SPN or trust related rather than a password problem.

title: Login failed for user
message: Login failed for user 'X'.
meaning: The client only ever sees State 1. The real state is in the error log and names the cause.

title: Login disabled
message: Login failed for user 'X'. Reason: The account is disabled.
meaning: The login exists and the password may even be right. It is switched off.

title: Cannot find server certificate
message: Cannot find server certificate with thumbprint 'X'.
meaning: A TDE-encrypted backup restored to an instance without the certificate. Restore the certificate first.

title: Certificate chain not trusted
message: The certificate chain was issued by an authority that is not trusted.
meaning: The client now validates the certificate by default. Your server did not change.
